text: The chronic changes in intramuscular fluid are an intriguing area of discussion. Without question, exercise training can promote an increase in glycogen stores. MacDougall and colleagues (124) reported that resting concentrations of glycogen increased by 66% after 5 months of regimented resistance training. Moreover, bodybuilders display double the glycogen content of those who do not participate in regular exercise (4). Such alterations would seem to be mediated both by enzymatic alterations and the greater storage capacity of larger muscles. The relevance to sarcoplasmic changes is that 1 g of glycogen attracts approximately 3 to 4 g of water (42, 159).
